title: ET Promethean Technologies FA26 (Module 5)
author: Andres Fortino (course deck, user-supplied)
locator: Slides 7-10 (quantum leap; decision points in speaker notes), 12-13 (printing press, internet cases), 15-16 and 19 (operational classification: Layers 1-3, six criteria), 17 (instrument flowchart), 20 (Long Fire timeline)
supports: Layer 1 system-vs-component; Layer 2 barrier statement and suppression test ('if the old state would simply return ... at most a breakthrough'); Layer 3 six criteria; single-tier dissolution = breakthrough, two or more tiers = Promethean candidate; 'irreversibility can only be verified after the fact'; mode: Confirmed vs Potential Promethean. Slide 20 lists Generative AI (2020s) as 'Potential Promethean' with a question mark.
does_not_support: Any measurement of agentic AI; the slide-20 exemplar label is a classroom illustration for generative AI, not evidence about the agent system evaluated here. Textbook Chapter 11 (section 11.2) was not supplied and is not claimed as read.

title: ET Invention Innovation Entrepreneurship FA26, Prep Lab 5
author: Andres Fortino (course deck, user-supplied)
supports: Criteria include breadth of impact, scale, paradigm shift, catalytic effects, democratization and the 10X idea; rapid investment or media attention is weak evidence; separate 'could this reshape society?' from 'is this useful for this organization?'; a potentially Promethean technology can be a poor choice for a particular application today.
does_not_support: Numeric thresholds beyond the 10X idea; any case-specific conclusion.

title: Assignment 3 Innovation and Disruption Agent v1.1 (prior specialist output)
author: Minghan Liu
supports: The SPS applicant-support proposal was classified as a proposed incremental, sustaining process innovation with Moderate conditional business-model exposure, and a three-way comparison (staff-only, simple retrieval, proposed agent) was recommended before any pilot.
does_not_support: Independent evidence; it is a prior AI-assisted student analysis used for continuity only.

title: General Purpose Technologies: 'Engines of Growth?'
author: Timothy F. Bresnahan and Manuel Trajtenberg
supports: General-purpose technologies are marked by pervasiveness, inherent potential for technical improvement and innovational complementarities; corroborates the course's 'widespread impact' and 'catalytic effect' criteria.
does_not_support: That any particular technology currently meets these criteria.

title: The Dynamo and the Computer: An Historical Perspective on the Modern Productivity Paradox
author: Paul A. David
date: 1990; American Economic Review 80(2) Papers and Proceedings
supports: Electrification produced large productivity gains only after factories were reorganized around the new technology, after a long lag; early small measured effects do not refute later transformation.
does_not_support: A prediction that agentic AI will follow the same path or timing.

title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
author: Tyna Eloundou, Sam Manning, Pamela Mishkin, Daniel Rock
supports: About 80% of the U.S. workforce could have at least 10% of tasks affected and about 19% could have at least 50% affected; LLMs 'exhibit traits of general-purpose technologies'.
does_not_support: Realized adoption, productivity or labor-market change. Exposure is potential, not dissolution. Three authors were OpenAI-affiliated.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
author: Thomas Kwa et al. (METR)
supports: Frontier 50%-task-completion time horizon about 50 minutes (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, early 2025); horizons have doubled roughly every seven months since 2019 and may have accelerated in 2024.
does_not_support: Real-world reliability outside the software task suite; the five-year extrapolation is a projection with stated external-validity limits.

title: The 2026 AI Index Report
author: Stanford HAI
supports: OSWorld agent accuracy rose from about 5% (2024) to 66.3% (2025), still below a 72.35% human baseline; generative AI reached 53% adoption within three years, faster than the internet or computers at the same stage; US AI investment $285.88 billion in 2025; a record 362 reported AI incidents in 2025.
does_not_support: Field reliability in consequential workflows; investment and adoption speed are not evidence of barrier dissolution (C2).

title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
author: Alexander Bick, Adam Blandin, David J. Deming
supports: Nearly 40% of U.S. adults aged 18-64 use generative AI; adoption faster than PCs and the internet. Generative AI assists only 1-5% of all work hours, with time savings of about 1.4% of total work hours.
does_not_support: Agent-specific use; organizational dependence; durable restructuring.

title: Generative AI at Work
author: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, Lindsey R. Raymond
date: NBER WP 31161 (2023); Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(2):889-942 (2025)
supports: An AI conversational assistant raised customer-support productivity 14% on average (issues resolved per hour) across 5,179 agents, 34% for novice and low-skilled workers, minimal for the most experienced: a measured gain and a skill-compression (democratizing) mechanism in a support setting analogous to applicant inquiries.
does_not_support: Autonomous agent performance (the tool assisted humans); higher-education transfer; barrier dissolution.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
author: Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Elizabeth Barnes, David Rein (METR)
supports: 16 experienced developers, 246 tasks: allowing AI tools increased completion time by 19%, while developers believed AI had cut time by 20%; perceived and measured effects can diverge sharply.
does_not_support: Effects of later tools or other occupations; small sample.

title: Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects (revised as 'Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI')
author: Anders Humlum and Emilie Vestergaard
supports: Danish linked survey and register data show precise null effects on earnings and recorded hours, ruling out effects larger than 2% two years after ChatGPT's launch, despite widespread employer chatbot initiatives.
does_not_support: Long-run effects, agentic systems specifically, or other labor markets.

title: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI
author: Daron Acemoglu
supports: Upper bound of about 0.66% total-factor-productivity gain over 10 years, adjusted to below 0.53%.
does_not_support: A ceiling on long-run transformation; it is a contested model-based estimate.

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
author: Frank F. Xu et al. (CMU and others)
supports: The most competitive agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks autonomously; more difficult long-horizon tasks remain beyond current systems.
does_not_support: Current frontier performance after the tested models; production reliability.

title: Gartner Predicts Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by End of 2027
author: Gartner
supports: Over 40% of agentic AI projects forecast to be canceled by end-2027 (cost, unclear value, risk controls); only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic AI' vendors judged real ('agent washing'); January 2025 poll of 3,412 webinar attendees: 19% significant investment, 42% conservative.
does_not_support: Measured outcomes; it is a forecast and a non-random poll. Gartner's 2028 adoption predictions are equally forecasts.

title: Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey press release
author: Stack Overflow
supports: 84% use or plan to use AI tools; 31% currently use AI agents, 17% plan to, 38% do not plan to; 46% do not trust the accuracy of AI output.
does_not_support: Representativeness of all developers; dependence or irreversibility.

title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation
author: Anthropic
supports: MCP donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI; more than 10,000 active public MCP servers and 97M+ monthly SDK downloads; adopted by ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, VS Code: an early catalytic/infrastructure signal.
does_not_support: Independent verification of counts; realized business value.

title: Building effective agents
author: Anthropic
locator: What are agents; When to use agents
supports: Workflows orchestrate LLMs and tools through predefined code paths; agents dynamically direct their own processes and tool use; agents trade latency and cost for performance and carry compounding-error risk; start with the simplest solution.
does_not_support: Independent evidence of agent superiority or reliability.

title: Google CEO: AI is more important than fire or electricity
author: CNBC (quoting Sundar Pichai)
date: 2018-02-01 (URL-dated); remark at a January 2018 town hall
supports: That a prominent executive said AI is 'more profound than ... electricity or fire'. Used only to test hype resistance.
does_not_support: Any classification. It is an opinion from an interested party, and it predates LLM agents.

title: NYU SPS Graduate Admissions
author: NYU School of Professional Studies
locator: Contact, appointments, information sessions, chatbot line
supports: Public admissions contact (212-998-7100, sps.admissions@nyu.edu), weekday appointments, Zoom information sessions, and 'For immediate assistance, try our chatbot, Violet.' The SPS baseline therefore already includes a public chatbot.
does_not_support: Violet's architecture, vendor, scope, tool use, accuracy or usage; internal workflows, costs or adoption posture.
